_README: HAND-CURATED benchmark. YOU fill this in by hand - do NOT use the AI to pick or label events.
The AI is only TESTED against this file later (experiments/eval_curated.py); it never helps build it.
For each event you research yourself:
move_date      - YYYY-MM-DD, the trading day the price actually tanked/surged.
direction      - 'tank' | 'surge' | 'calm'  (calm = a control day, no real event).
label_type     - 'event' (real news catalyst) | 'calm' (control) | 'unexplained' (big move, NO clear news).
catalyst       - short phrase describing the real cause (e.g. 'Q2 earnings miss + weak guidance').
headlines      - the PRE-MOVE news you found. Each: title, url, published (ISO timestamp).
IMPORTANT: only include headlines published BEFORE the move (overnight/pre-market
or the days before). A post-move 'here is why it fell' article is lookahead - do NOT use it.
For 'calm' and 'unexplained' rows, leave headlines empty [].
why            - one line, YOUR reasoning for how this news caused the move.
expected_verdict - what the agent SHOULD say: 'caution'/'reject' for real events, 'trust' for calm days.
Aim for ~15-40 rows, roughly balanced between 'event' and 'calm', plus a few 'unexplained' if you find them.
Delete the two _example rows below (they are skipped anyway) once you have real ones.

events.catalyst: Q2 earnings miss and weak delivery guidance

headlines.title: Tesla Q2 earnings miss estimates, warns on deliveries

events.why: Earnings missed and guidance was cut after the close; the stock gapped down at the next open.
